T7-01.claim: Actual start_new_session=True guard authenticates with the real scheduler and emits registered; existing session leaders do not call setsid again.

T7-02.claim: Cooperative frame/PID/group SIGINT and SIGTERM reap the direct child before the real DRAINING CAS; exit is 128+requested signal. Forced own-group SIGKILL produces no handoff or draining notification.

T7-03.claim: Real orphan completion drains with no later attempt; closed-control fd is removed from reads/selects, and driver records at most one EOF read.

T7-04.claim: Invalid active nonce/run/oversize/truncated controls cancel and reap before handoff. EOF/reset suppress undeliverable notifications while preserving authenticated DRAINING. Unexpected scheduler errors are contained.

T7-05.claim: One bounded compound deadline spans setup and all attempts; a fake-clock test proves setup plus first attempt exhaust it before a later spawn. Partial controls do not block the active execution deadline.

T7-06.claim: TERM-ignoring group grandchild is killed at grace expiry even after direct-child exit. Actual observed setsid escape remains untouched and scheduler charge stays UNCERTAIN; separate-session controller sentinel survives. Group scan is cleanup guidance only, never absence proof.

T7-07.claim: Real fixture-domain enqueue/poll/register/drain/recovery, late revoked-grant refusal, six independent admission clients at budgets 1 and 4, group presence until guard reap, live finalizer retention, and incomplete orphan recovery under explicit 10s/30s targets and 45s watchdog.

T7-08.claim: Logical invoking controller is SIGKILLed at manifest/register/registered/fork/run/drain/drained barriers. Control descriptor closure comes from actual controller death. Guard stays a direct harness child so its exit can be waited without depending on init. No work starts after observed EOF. Post-drain live-caller retention and dead-caller incomplete recovery are demonstrated.

T7-09.claim: Oversized/truncated/malformed manifests and wrong nonce/run/kind/payload/oversized/truncated controls cannot authorize launch. Manifest trailing bytes reject. Child verifies private fds closed, literal argv/env and inherited stdout/stderr. Unread notifications hit bounded send deadline and close spawning.

T7-10.claim: Requested 2/15 is forwarded and returned as 130/143. Real signals before manifest/during registration, active PID/group delivery, queued controller-group signals, and controller-group-to-private-cancel forwarding are covered. These are fixture controllers, not Task 11 CLI acceptance.

secure_by_spec.state: Controller death at named barriers, repeated/group cancellation, direct-child reap before drain, failed handoff, forced-kill no handoff, uncertainty retention and recovery.

task11_handoff.ordinary_exit: DRAINING CAS and matching in-band frame are provisional only. Guard exit 0 does not imply runner pass. Missing executable/setup failure/zero launched attempts require Task 11 to inspect actual runner facts.
task11_handoff.cancel: Cooperative cancellation emits raw child facts then authenticated draining and exits 128+signal; execution-timeout is a typed Problem, not inferred solely from raw child exit.
task11_handoff.forced_or_failed_handoff: SIGKILL, failed scheduler handoff or unavailable control notification is not a successful execution. Guard cannot notify after killing itself. Independent quiescence/recovery must keep missing outcomes incomplete.
task11_handoff.orphan: After EOF/reset, current child is reaped, later spawning closes, and scheduler DRAINING can commit without a notification; no durable final outcome/baseline is fabricated.
task11_handoff.ownership: Caller owns guard reaping, non-signalling post-reap ESRCH plus observed-escape absence, FINALIZING/source checks/publication/release. Existing scheduler recovery is exercised without changing scheduler.py.
residual_risks: Observation immediately before Popen cannot atomically prevent controller death between the check and fork. The newly added post-phase check narrows this inherent race; the registered group remains charged if it occurs.
A bounded group snapshot is only cancellation cleanup guidance. It does not establish quiescence, arbitrary daemon containment, or absence of an unobserved escaped descendant.
Linux evidence only. No macOS lifecycle run, real Task 11 CLI/end-to-end final publication, or full-suite/release gate was performed.
